language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide of $732-746m, less Q1 $173.0m, Q2 $183.3m and the Q3 guide of $184-190m, implies Q4 2026 revenue of about $185.7-205.7m (midpoint $195.7m). Against Q4 2025's $172.6m that is about +13% at the midpoint, down from 18% guided for Q3 and 23% reported in Q2. On the Q2 call management also flagged a harder Q4 net-retention comparison. findings.finding: Fastly has beaten the midpoint of its own revenue guide in each recent quarter: Q2 came in at $183.3m against a $170-176m guide, $10m above the midpoint. Benzinga/Zacks history shows revenue surprises of +0.7% to +7% over the last four quarters. Q3 consensus of about $187.6m sits at the guide midpoint, so another beat is likely. The CFO said under half of the Q2 upside was episodic (World Cup, with 75% of games in Q2) and that the Q3 guide is otherwise normal Q2-to-Q3 seasonality.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats were sold in Q1 2026 (-38.2%) and Q2 2026 (-12.9%), and bought in Q4 2025 (+72.3%), Q3 2025 (+35.9%) and Q2 2025 (+14.4%) (baseline). The reported-quarter beat has not been the deciding line in 2026.

Any disclosure in Q3 of a top-customer traffic shift would be a large negative. No dated report of such a shift was found.

findings.finding: Memory-cost inflation is a gross-margin and capex risk. F5 guided its FY27 gross margin lower on higher component costs on 2026-10-28.

findings.finding: Q2 revenue is set up for a beat on a bar the company itself set. Management guided Q2 total net sales growth in the mid-30s (about $457-471M on a $343.9M base), explicitly including pipeline shipments for rhode's Sephora Europe launch. The CEO said 'all that pipeline is going to go out in Q2' and that they were 'taking an even stronger stance on the pipeline' given prior Rhode launches. Rhode launched on 2026-09-30 in 500+ Sephora stores across 19 European countries. In Q1 Rhode contributed about $160M and 'outperformed our expectations', and total Q1 revenue of $479.4M beat a $425.7-428M consensus by about 12%. Consensus of $467-471M sits at the top of the guided band, not above it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-08-05): revenue beat by about 12%, plus a raise, gave +6.88%. Q4 FY26 (2026-05-20) gave +4.73%. Revenue beats have been bought and sold depending on the guide.

findings.finding: The FY27 guide leaves arithmetic room for a second raise. The $1,938-1,968M guide is +18-20%, which implies a FY26 base of about $1,642M. Prior-year quarters are Q1 $353.7M, Q2 $343.9M and Q3 $489.5M, so prior-year Q4 was about $455M. FY27 Q1 was $479.4M and Q2 is guided to about $464-471M. That leaves an implied H2 of about $990-1,020M, or +5% to +8% on a $945M prior-year H2, once Rhode is annualised (August). Management separately said organic growth for the balance of the year would be 10-12% and that 'all brands grow' (my derivation from the 2026-08-05 release and call). Last time the raise (+$100M of sales) exceeded the Q1 beat (about $50M).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raise in Aug 2026 gave +6.88%. FY27 first guide in May 2026 gave +4.73%. Raise in Feb 2026 gave -9.18%, sold on core-brand quality. The Nov 2025 guide disappointment gave -35.04%. Guidance is the line this stock trades on, in both directions.

findings.finding: A counterparty reading on the core e.l.f. brand points softer than management's 'improving trends'. Ulta reported its quarter ended 2026-08-01 on 2026-08-27, after e.l.f.'s last call. It said mass makeup sales declined in the low single digits as brands lapped big launches, and cosmetics fell to 37% of its sales from 38%. e.l.f. Cosmetics is the largest mass color brand. This overlaps only July of e.l.f.'s Sep quarter. Ulta is one channel, and management said e.l.f.'s fall innovation held 4 of the top 10 new launches in mass cosmetics.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Core-brand weakness drove the large negatives: Nov 2025 -35.04% and Feb 2026 -9.18%, the latter despite a total-revenue beat (https://www.tipranks.com/news/e-l-f-beauty-stock-elf-plunges-as-intl-sales-slow-outlook-disappoints-wall-street describes the international and outlook reaction).

So September-quarter unit volume on most of the e.l.f. line faces a price step-up versus July.
